chapter: Leaving the band, Strayhorn and reflections
title: Duke's modesty: 'I love you madly' and not believing you're great
summary: Greer recalls Duke's advice not to let praise go to his head.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: That's why he said -- he coined a phrase, 'I love you madly,' you remember.
He would say, 'I love you madly.' He used to say that after each performance. 'Good night, I love you madly.' That's right. And he meant that. You know, people fawning on him.

I remember one time he said to me, he said, 'Sonny, don't ever let nobody tell you how great you are. Keep climbing. Just thank the Lord and lady luck has her arms around you. Don't ever let them because it's always somebody can duplicate it. Don't ever'-- and I don't. It sounds good but it don't mean -- hell, I can't do anything somebody else can't do. I laugh, I don't say it to nobody's face, but it's stupid. American people, invariably use it, they use the term so loosely.
And genius, they use that a lot, too. They call anybody a genius, it don't make no difference in the end.

Yeah, there's nothing in the world that ain't been duplicated, nothing. They duplicate the atomic bomb, didn't they? They went on and made bigger and better. At first that was the greatest weapon in the world, just like ham and eggs now. Everybody got one.
